text.insert: says what the run measured. It holds the git head and changed-file count of the app and the design system. It also holds the Chromium build, the axe-core version and sha256, and up to 50 blocked requests and WebSockets.
computes every number in the report. One formula runs at the page, area and app level.
A check fails when any finding is a fail in any theme or viewport. Else it warns when any finding warns, else it passes.
A check that did not run, or that the page skips, is n/a and is left out.
Pass counts 1, warn 0.5 and fail 0. The page score is the mean over the applicable checks, times 100.
For example, 20 applicable checks with 16 passes, 2 warns and 2 fails give (16 + 1) / 20 × 100 = 85.
Each of the 6 areas applies the page formula to its own checks. The app's area score is the mean of the page area scores where the area applies.
The app score is the mean of the page scores. A page with no score is left out of the mean.
A skipped optional page gets no score. A page where no browser check ran gets no score too, because the static checks alone would raise the app score.

Raise a Score One Fix at a Time

The hill-climb loop raises the score in small steps, and each step proves itself. Start with a full baseline and a quick baseline, because a quick run sees fewer themes and viewports and scores higher.

bun run design:score --app knowledge-system --label base
bun run design:score --app knowledge-system --quick --label base-quick
Pick the worst fail in the base report. That is the check with the most fail pages in the Checks table.
Fix that one finding in the app.
